newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil soars, traders puzzled.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil soars, traders puzzled.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps rose sharply in late afternoon trading on Thursday on large purchases by financial insitutions and majors, some of which were on the back of an East-West play, traders said.
"The market went crazy at around lunch time when the Wall Streeters and a few majors came in to buy," one trader said.
August swaps were last quoted at $23.30/$23.40 per barrel, up almost $1.00 from Tuesday's $22.40/$22.50 per barrel, brokers said.
August traded earlier in the day at $23.30, $23.35 and $23.40 before easing to current levels, they said.
September was last quoted at $23.70/$23.90, from Tuesday's $23.10/$23.20.

As a result, the August/September narrowed further to last trade at minus 44 cents and 48 cents from an earlier in the day deal of minus 50 cents which was 20 cents under an early week trade of minus 70 cents, brokers said.
Most players were hard pressed to explain the latest surge in prices with many blaming it on technicals.
"Everybody joined in the buying this afternoon. The market is hyped up," another trader said.
Most felt that the market fundamentals do not support such a big increase and they were expecting some form of correction either later this week or early next week.
"China is still not buying and the tanks are still full in Singapore. I don't see any reason for prices to increase so much," a trader said.
August gas oil swaps were trading at around $21.50 late on Friday giving the market an almost $2.00 per barrel hike in less than one week.

The rise was partly due to renewed physical buying interest in the local spot market where on Wednesday, one 150,000-barrel cargo for August 7-10 lifting traded at $21.90 per barrel, up $1.00 from Monday's lowest traded level.
On Monday, four deals totalling 670,000 barrels were done between $20.90 and $21.20 per barrel on a free-on-board Singapore basis.
Meanwhile, the fuel oil market was steady with August last quoted at $98.75/$99.50, brokers said.
